analysis:
Examined the MediaIngest.swift change (head lines 769-777 and 798-802) and the GLM5NextMediaRoutingTests.swift additions.

The only production change replaces the inline-video data-URI header check with a lowercase allow-list (`admittedVideoDataURIHeaders`). It now admits `data:video/x-m4v;base64` and `data:video/mov;base64` alongside mp4 and quicktime. Comparison is still exact on the portion before the first comma, case-insensitive via lowercasing, and base64-only.

All later controls are unchanged:
- `dataFromDataURI` enforces the decoded-byte cap before allocation (lines 890-938).
- `MemoryBackedVideoAsset` is memory-backed with no plaintext temp file, so the T-050 posture is preserved.
- `MediaProcessing.metadata` and `enforceVideoLimits` enforce duration, per-frame pixel, per-request video count and aggregate frame-pixel caps, all failing closed (lines 786-885).
- Non-`data:` URIs are still rejected (SSRF and local-file-read guard).

The added labels only widen label acceptance, because the container is sniffed from the bytes. They add no new fetch path, no new file write and no new logging of request-derived content. The error text is a static string and stays in-process. I found no change to the A-001 confidentiality, TB-002 or TB-007 boundaries. No impact on the T-041 prefix-cache surface.

The test file adds a CryptoKit import, a stub tokenizer, a helper that reads fixture clips from the repo (SHA-256 verified), and a test that runs readiness videos through the scheduler path. Tests only, no production exposure. The test patch excerpt is truncated and I did not see the full test file.

Residual question: AVFoundation parsing of the newly admitted QuickTime/variable-frame-rate inputs is a native attack surface that was already reachable via the quicktime label, so it is not new. Only unit-level review was done; the unchanged `MemoryBackedVideoAsset` and `MediaProcessing.metadata` implementations were not supplied.
